articles.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
articles.selectionReason: Open full-text paper; topic brain_computer_interface; quality signal passed; application scenario is clear.

paperCard.problem: 目前语音脑机接口（让机器读懂大脑活动并翻译成语言）的研究缺少统一的尺子。不同团队用不同的数据集、采集方法、说话方式和词表，得出来的分数没法互相比较，所以很难判断哪个系统真的进步了。
paperCard.method: 论文提出要设计一种通用的沟通度量标准，统一衡量系统在目标词汇分布上能传达多少信息。先把“用户应能说出哪些词”定义清楚，再计算系统从这些词中成功传递了多少信息。
paperCard.difference: 以前的研究各自用一套评测方式，比如词错误率、句子准确率等，因为设置不同结果难以对比。这篇论文强调先统一“沟通目标”和“信息量”，而不是只看某个系统的单独表现。
paperCard.innovation: 创新点是把测量对象从“系统内部指标”转为“用户与系统之间的信息传递”，并明确把词汇分布和传达的信息量作为两大核心问题，为不同设备之间的比较给出共同参照。
paperCard.implementation: 摘要中没有给出数学公式或实验细节，但大致路径是：先定义一个标准的词汇分布（即用户可能想说的词的范围），再通过实验让系统翻译神经信号，最后计算该系统从该分布中成功传递了多少信息比特。
paperCard.applications: 可用于比较不同语音脑机接口系统的真实沟通效率，帮助研究团队选择更有潜力的算法；长远看服务于瘫痪、失语患者的日常交流，也可能用于新型人机交互。
technicalTerms: 语音脑机接口（speech BCI）：直接读取大脑神经活动并将其翻译成语言的技术
神经活动（neural activity）：大脑中神经细胞产生的电信号，能反映说话意图
词汇分布（distribution of words）：用户可能想说的各种词语及其出现概率
信息（information）：系统正确传达的语言内容量，通常可用信息论中的比特衡量

articles.highlight: 该领域缺乏统一的进展衡量标准，因为不同系统使用不同数据集、记录方法、语音类型和词汇，导致分数难以比较。
articles.summary: 论文指出语音脑机接口领域缺乏统一的进展衡量标准，因为系统在数据集、记录方法、语音类型和词汇上各不相同，报告分数几乎不可比。研究者还提出需要回答两个问题：用户应该能表达什么样的词分布，以及系统能传达其中多少信息。文章值得一读，因为它为解决测评混乱提供了一种通用思路。
articles.failureAnalysis: 作为arXiv预印本，论文尚未经过同行评审，且方法细节和实验结果未在摘要中展示，无法判断其度量方案是否实际可用。
articles.sourceExcerpt: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain–Computer Interfaces Dulhan Jayalath Benjamin Ballyk Oiwi Parker Jones Neural Processing Lab (PNPL ), University of Oxford Abstract Speech brain–computer interfaces (speech BCIs) translate neural activity into language, offering a path towards restoring speech for people with paralysis and, more broadly, enabling new forms of natural human–computer interaction. Despite this promise, the field lacks a common measure of progress because systems use different datasets, recording methods, types of speech, and vo- cabularies, so their reported scores are rarely comparable. Underlying this measurement problem are two unresolved questions: (i) what distribution of words should a speech BCI enable a user to communicate, and (ii) how much information from this distribution can a system convey.

paperCard.problem: 目前语音脑机接口（让机器读懂大脑活动并翻译成语言）的研究缺少统一的尺子。不同团队用不同的数据集、采集方法、说话方式和词表，得出来的分数没法互相比较，所以很难判断哪个系统真的进步了。
paperCard.method: 论文提出要设计一种通用的沟通度量标准，统一衡量系统在目标词汇分布上能传达多少信息。先把“用户应能说出哪些词”定义清楚，再计算系统从这些词中成功传递了多少信息。
paperCard.difference: 以前的研究各自用一套评测方式，比如词错误率、句子准确率等，因为设置不同结果难以对比。这篇论文强调先统一“沟通目标”和“信息量”，而不是只看某个系统的单独表现。
paperCard.innovation: 创新点是把测量对象从“系统内部指标”转为“用户与系统之间的信息传递”，并明确把词汇分布和传达的信息量作为两大核心问题，为不同设备之间的比较给出共同参照。
paperCard.implementation: 摘要中没有给出数学公式或实验细节，但大致路径是：先定义一个标准的词汇分布（即用户可能想说的词的范围），再通过实验让系统翻译神经信号，最后计算该系统从该分布中成功传递了多少信息比特。
paperCard.applications: 可用于比较不同语音脑机接口系统的真实沟通效率，帮助研究团队选择更有潜力的算法；长远看服务于瘫痪、失语患者的日常交流，也可能用于新型人机交互。
technicalTerms: 语音脑机接口（speech BCI）：直接读取大脑神经活动并将其翻译成语言的技术
神经活动（neural activity）：大脑中神经细胞产生的电信号，能反映说话意图
词汇分布（distribution of words）：用户可能想说的各种词语及其出现概率
信息（information）：系统正确传达的语言内容量，通常可用信息论中的比特衡量

en.highlight: The field lacks a common measure of progress because systems use different datasets, recording methods, types of speech, and vocabularies, so their reported scores are rarely comparable.
en.summary: This paper argues that speech brain-computer interfaces lack a common measure of progress because systems vary in datasets, recording methods, speech types, and vocabularies, making reported scores hard to compare. The authors identify two core questions: what word distribution a user should be able to communicate, and how much information a system can convey from it. It is worth reading because it offers a unified way to evaluate progress in a fragmented field.
en.failureAnalysis: As an arXiv preprint, it has not yet undergone peer review, and no methodological details or experimental results are visible from the abstract, so the practical feasibility of the metric remains unclear.
en.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces

paperCard.problem: Speech brain-computer interfaces need a common yardstick. Different teams use different datasets, recording methods, speaking styles, and vocabularies, so scores cannot be compared; it is hard to tell which system is actually making progress.
paperCard.method: The paper proposes designing a common communication metric that standardizes the target word distribution and measures how much information a system transmits from that distribution.
paperCard.difference: Older approaches each use idiosyncratic evaluation setups and scores. This paper shifts the focus to a shared notion of user communication goals and conveyed information, enabling fairer comparisons.
paperCard.innovation: It reframes measurement from system-specific metrics to user-system information transfer and explicitly highlights word distribution and conveyed information as the two core problems.
paperCard.implementation: The abstract gives no formulas or experiments, but the likely path is: define a standard distribution of words a user would want to say, record neural signals, decode them with the BCI, and compute how many information bits are correctly transmitted from that distribution.
paperCard.applications: Comparing different speech BCI systems, guiding algorithm development, restoring communication for paralyzed or speech-impaired people, and enabling new forms of natural human-computer interaction.
technicalTerms: speech BCI: a technology that reads neural activity and translates it into language
neural activity: electrical signals from brain cells that reflect speaking intentions
distribution of words: the set of possible words a user may want to say, with their probabilities
information: the language content correctly conveyed by the system, often measured in bits using information theory

articles.title: EEG-based Visual Retrieval and Reconstruction: From Neurally Visible Optimal Layer to Hierarchical Diffusion Generation

paperCard.problem: 用脑电 EEG 识别或重建人正在看的内容时，旧方法把脑电信号和图片高级语义直接拉到一起比对，但脑电信号其实分不同层次，不同视觉信息在脑电里的清晰程度不一样，直接对齐会错位，也浪费信息。
paperCard.method: 它先把 EEG 映射到某个“神经可见最优层”，选出脑电里最能看清视觉成分的特征层；然后用这个特征去检索图片，或者作为条件，用分层扩散生成逐步从粗到细重建图像。
paperCard.difference: 旧方法是一股脑对齐，没有区分视觉信息的层次；这个工作明确利用了 EEG 信号的多层次性质，先找合适的层，再用扩散模型分层生成，而不是一次性输出结果。
paperCard.innovation: 创新点在于提出“神经可见最优层”的概念并使用分层扩散生成：即不是所有视觉成分都同等出现在脑电里，要挑出可见度最高的那一层来配合生成，从而减少跨模态错配。
paperCard.implementation: 具体步骤摘要里没有细说，但逻辑是：先处理 EEG 信号，确定哪个中间特征层的神经可见性最好；让 EEG 特征与预训练视觉模型在这个层对齐，完成视觉检索；再用扩散作为生成模型，按“高层语义→细节纹理”的分层方式重建图像。
paperCard.applications: 可以用于脑机接口（BCI）中的视觉类型识别、基于意念的图像搜索、辅助交流与康复评估，也能帮助理解人脑如何处理视觉信息。
technicalTerms: EEG：脑电，用贴在头皮上的电极记录大脑电活动，时间分辨率高但空间模糊。
BCI：脑机接口，让人脑直接与计算机等设备通信。
神经可见最优层：指脑电中不同视觉信息能被明显观测到的某个特征阶段，选这一层做对齐最好。
跨模态不匹配：脑电和图像特征不是同一个来源，直接硬套会导致两边对应不上。
分层扩散生成：一种图像生成方式，先大致生成整体结构，再逐步细化细节。

articles.sourceExcerpt: 1 EEG-based Visual Retrieval and Reconstruction: From Neurally Visible Optimal Layer to Hierarchical Diffusion Generation Minyi Wang, Zhenqin Wu and Rihui Li Abstract—Decoding visual perception from electroencephalog- raphy (EEG) is important for non-invasive brain-computer in- terfaces (BCIs). However, most existing visual decoding pipelines directly align EEG features with semantic features from pre- trained vision models. Those EEG signals carry information at more than one level and this practice disregards the varying neural visibility of different visual components in EEG signals, leading to cross modal mismatches and incomplete information use.

en.highlight: Most visual decoding pipelines directly align EEG features with semantic features, ignoring varying neural visibility, causing cross-modal mismatch and incomplete information use.
en.summary: This paper studies retrieving and reconstructing visual percepts from EEG, arguing that direct alignment to pretrained vision features ignores the multi-level nature of EEG and component-specific neural visibility. The authors propose starting from a neurally visible optimal layer then applying hierarchical diffusion generation to reduce mismatch. The topic is closely tied to brain-computer interfaces and visual decoding, though the current evidence is limited.
en.failureAnalysis: Only the abstract is available; there are no experimental results, quantitative comparisons, or model details yet. Claims cannot be verified without the full paper.
en.title: EEG-based Visual Retrieval and Reconstruction: From Neurally Visible Optimal Layer to Hierarchical Diffusion Generation

paperCard.problem: When decoding what a person sees from EEG, older methods directly match EEG signals to high-level image semantics, ignoring that different visual components are not equally visible in EEG, causing mismatches and wasted information.
paperCard.method: It maps EEG into an optimally visible neural layer, then uses these aligned features for visual retrieval or as conditions for a hierarchical diffusion generator that produces images from coarse to fine.
paperCard.difference: Unlike older methods that align features globally, this work exploits the layered nature of EEG by selecting the most visible layer first and generating hierarchically rather than at once.
paperCard.innovation: The innovation is the idea of a neurally visible optimal layer combined with hierarchical diffusion generation, avoiding treating all visual components equally and reducing cross-modal mismatches.
paperCard.implementation: Specifics are not disclosed in the abstract: the general pipeline is to determine the best neural layer from EEG, align EEG with vision model features at that layer, then use diffusion generation in a hierarchical manner to synthesize the image.
paperCard.applications: Non-invasive brain-computer interfaces, imagined-image retrieval, assistive communication, rehabilitation evaluation, and studying how the brain represents visual information.
technicalTerms: EEG: Electroencephalography, recording brain electrical activity from the scalp with high time resolution.
BCI: Brain-computer interface, enabling direct communication between the brain and devices.
Neurally visible optimal layer: The feature stage where different visual components are most reliably observed in EEG, chosen for cross-modal alignment.
Cross-modal mismatch: The feature distributions of EEG and image are different, so direct alignment leads to poor correspondence.
Hierarchical diffusion generation: A generation method that first builds the overall structure and then refines details step by step.
